name: Daniel K. Inouye International Airport
before:
Hawaii's main airport, three miles north west of downtown Honolulu, and the hub for Hawaiian Airlines. It offers non-stop flights across North America, Asia and Oceania.

The site is enormous, covering more than one per cent of the whole island of Oahu.

Its runways are genuinely unusual. There are four major runways, operated jointly with the adjacent Hickam Air Force Base, and the principal one, 8R/26L, is known as the Reef Runway. Completed in 1977, it was the world's first major runway built entirely offshore, and was a designated alternate landing site for the Space Shuttle. Beyond the paved runways there are two marked offshore waterways for seaplanes.

There are 60 gates across three terminals, 54 with jet bridges and six hard stands. Terminals 1 and 2 are connected after security, which is worth knowing for a connection.

The airport is named after Daniel Inouye, a Honolulu native, Medal of Honor recipient and senator for Hawaii from 1963 until his death in 2012.
after:
Hawaii's main airport, north west of downtown Honolulu. It is a hub for Hawaiian Airlines and handles more than 21 million passengers a year, with non-stop flights across North America, Asia and Oceania.

Its four runways are shared with the neighbouring Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam. The Reef Runway, completed in 1977, was the world's first major runway built entirely offshore. Beyond the paved runways there are two marked offshore waterways for seaplanes.

There are three terminals. Hawaiian Airlines checks in its inter-island flights at Terminal 1, Mokulele Airlines uses the commuter Terminal 3 and the other airlines check in at Terminal 2. Terminals 1 and 2 are connected after security, which is worth knowing for a connection.

The airport is named after Daniel Inouye, a Honolulu native, Medal of Honor recipient and senator for Hawaii from 1963 until his death in 2012.

claims.claim: north west of downtown Honolulu
claims.note: Was 'three miles north west'. The coordinates put the airport 4.4 miles in a straight line from the GeoNames centre, so three miles is a ratio of 0.68 and fails the check. The FAA master record gives '03 NW', which is three NAUTICAL miles (about 3.5 statute miles) from the business district to the airport reference point, so the two written sources do not agree on the unit and the figure goes. The bearing stays: Wikipedia and the FAA both say north west, and the computed 280 degrees is west, one point away.

claims.claim: a hub for Hawaiian Airlines
claims.note: Was 'the hub'. The caller asked how the airline describes the service now that Hawaiian is in the Alaska Air Group. Hawaiian's own release of 18 September 2026 calls Honolulu and Kahului 'the company's two largest Hawaii hubs' and announces Alaska-branded 737s on Honolulu to Kahului from 3 October; its About page says Hawaiian has combined passenger service systems with Alaska Airlines and that Hawaiian flights stay Hawaiian-branded. No independent page on the ownership could be saved (transportation.gov answered 403; the Maui Now report of August 2025 reprints the airline's release), so the text says only what both sources support: a hub for Hawaiian.

claims.claim: more than 21 million passengers a year
claims.inAfter: handles more than 21 million passengers a year
claims.note: Added at the caller's request for a traffic line, in place of the site-size line (cut below) as the measure of how big it is. TOTAL passengers, arrivals plus departures: the operator's live page says more than 21 million enplaned and deplaned a year, and Wikipedia's infobox gives 21,985,522 for 2025, sourced to the state. The state's own 2025 table is a Tableau dashboard that draws its figures as an image (updated 17 September 2026), so it could not be saved as text. The FAA's preliminary CY2025 table counts 10,430,353 revenue enplanements (boardings only, about half of total passengers), down 0.18 per cent, consistent with it.
